title: Big 12 Conference Championship Game: How Texas Tech clinched a berth
summary: Update: With a win over TCU on Thanksgiving night, Texas. Tech clinched a spot in the Big 12 Championship Game against Utah. Rivalry Week is upon us. While some teams are already looking ahead to the College Football Playoff, others are hoping to play spoiler during Rivalry Week. But that proposition has taken on greater […]
content: (Photo by Jocelyn Rafidi/Baylor Athletics/University Images via Getty Images) Update: With a win over TCU on Thanksgiving night, Texas. Tech clinched a spot in the Big 12 Championship Game against Utah. Rivalry Week is upon us. While some teams are already looking ahead to the College Football Playoff, others are hoping to play spoiler during Rivalry Week. But that proposition has taken on greater importance this year, with the impending move to a 24-team playoff next season. That means these are the last round of Conference Championship Games, so denying a rival a spot in the title game might mean even more this year. In the Big 12, unbeaten Utah has already clinched a spot in the title game. But who will the Utes face: No. 11 Texas Tech, or No. 10 BYU? How Texas Tech can clinch a spot The Red Raiders have the inside track to a spot in the Big 12 title game, and a date with Utah. With a win over TCU on Thanksgiving night, then Texas Tech will clinch the second spot in the Big 12 Championship Game. However, the Red Raiders can still get in if they lose to TCU, provided BYU loses to Cincinnati on Saturday afternoon. How BYU can clinch a spot BYU hosts Cincinnati on Saturday afternoon, but the Cougars might already be eliminated before kickoff. To advance to the Big 12 title game, BYU needs Texas Tech to lose to TCU on Thursday night, and then a win over Cincinnati on Saturday.

title: Big Ten Championship Game scenarios and tiebreakers
summary: Update (Friday afternoon): With Iowa’s dominant win over Nebraska, the Hawkeyes are still alive for a spot in the Big Ten Championship Game. In addition, any scenario where an Iowa win helps another team is still on the tableThe final Big Ten Championship Game is just around the corner, ahead of next season’s move to […]
content: (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Update (Friday afternoon): With Iowa’s dominant win over Nebraska, the Hawkeyes are still alive for a spot in the Big Ten Championship Game. In addition, any scenario where an Iowa win helps another team is still on the tableThe final Big Ten Championship Game is just around the corner, ahead of next season’s move to a 24-team College Football Playoff. In addition, Iowa’s win has eliminated both USC and Ohio State from contention. However, what two teams will play in that game is far from unsettled. Entering Rivalry Week six — yes six — teams still have a chance to clinch one of the two spots in the Big Ten Championship Game. Those six teams (UCLA, Iowa, Oregon, USC, Ohio State, and Indiana) have much different paths to Indianapolis. But they each have a path. Here are the scenarios and tiebreakers you need to know ahead of the weekend. Big Ten Standings First, here is how those six teams stack up in the standings: 1. UCLA (10-1 overall, 7-1 in conference) 2. Indiana (9-2 overall, 6-2 in conference) 3. Iowa (9-2 overall, 6-2 in conference) 4. Oregon (8-3 overall, 6-2 in conference) 5. USC (8-3 overall, 5-3 in conference) 6. Ohio State (7-4 overall, 5-3 in conference) Yes, all six of these teams could get into the title game. How UCLA clinches a Big Ten berth UCLA has the easiest path to a spot in the Big Ten Championship Game. With a win over USC on Saturday afternoon, the Bruins are in. However, UCLA can back into the Big Ten Championship Game a few different ways: An Indiana loss to Purdue AND an Iowa loss to Nebraska, OR An Indiana loss to Purdue AND an Oregon loss to Washington, OR An Iowa loss to Nebraska AND an Oregon loss to Washington, OR An Iowa win against Nebraska AND an Oregon win against Washington AND an Indiana loss to Purdue, OR An Indiana win against Purdue AND an Iowa win against Nebraska AND an Oregon loss to Washington AND either a win by Minnesota against Wisconsin OR an Ohio State win against Michigan, OR (Stay with me now) Wins by: Illinois against Northwestern AND Indiana against Purdue AND Iowa against Nebraska AND Maryland against Penn State AND Michigan against Ohio State AND Michigan State against Rutgers AND Wisconsin against Minnesota AND an Oregon loss to Washington AND a higher SportSource Analytics metric score than Iowa Got it? Good, because we are just getting started. And remember, this was the team with the easiest path. How Oregon clinches a Big Ten berth Here is how the Ducks advance to the Big Ten Championship Game: A win against Washington AND an Iowa loss to Nebraska, OR A win against Washington AND a UCLA win against USC, OR A win against Washington AND an Indiana win against Purdue, OR An Ohio State win against Michigan AND an Indiana loss against Purdue AND an Iowa loss against Nebraska AND a USC loss against UCLA AND a Wisconsin loss to Minnesota, OR An Indiana loss against Purdue AND an Iowa loss against Nebraska AND an Ohio State loss against Michigan AND a USC loss against UCLA AND a Wisconsin loss against Minnesota, OR A Michigan State win against Rutgers AND an Ohio State win against Michigan AND a Wisconsin win against Minnesota AND an Indiana loss to Purdue AND an Iowa loss to Nebraska AND a USC loss to UCLA, OR A Wisconsin win against Minnesota AND an Indiana loss to Purdue AND an Iowa loss to Nebraska AND an Ohio State loss to Michigan AND a USC loss to UCLA We will catch our breath next, moving to the team with the toughest road to Indianapolis. How Ohio State clinches a Big Ten berth Update (Friday afternoon): With Iowa’s win over Nebraska, the Buckeyes have been eliminated. Previously: The road is daunting for the Buckeyes, who enter Rivalry Week with a 7-4 record overall. But they have a slim chance at a spot in the Big Ten Championship Game. Ohio State punches their ticket if: They beat Michigan AND Maryland beats Penn State AND Rutgers beats Michigan State AND Wisconsin beats Minnesota AND Indiana loses to Purdue AND Iowa loses to Nebraska AND Oregon loses to Washington AND USC loses to UCLA. So you’re saying there’s a chance … How Indiana clinches a Big Ten berth The Hoosiers can head back to the Big Ten Championship Game with a win and some help. Indiana punches a ticked to Indianapolis with: A win against Purdue AND an Iowa loss to Nebraska AND an Oregon loss to Washington, OR A win against Purdue AND an Oregon win against Washington AND an Iowa loss to Nebraska AND a UCLA loss to USC, OR A win against Purdue AND an Iowa win against Nebraska AND a UCLA loss to USC AND an Oregon loss to Washington, OR A win against Purdue AND an Iowa win against Nebraska AND a Minnesota win against Wisconsin AND an Oregon win against Washington AND a UCLA loss to USC How Iowa clinches a Big Ten berth Here is how the Hawkeyes can clinch a spot in the Big Ten Championship Game: A win against Nebraska AND an Indiana loss to Purdue AND an Oregon loss to Washington, OR A win against Nebraska AND an Oregon win against Washington AND an Indiana loss to Purdue AND a UCLA loss to USC, OR A win against Nebraska AND an Indiana win against Purdue AND an Oregon win against Washington AND a Wisconsin win against Minnesota AND a UCLA loss to USC, OR A win against Nebraska AND an Indiana loss against Purdue AND an Oregon loss against Washington AND a UCLA loss against USC, OR A win against Nebraska AND an Indiana win against Purdue AND a Michigan win against Ohio State AND a Wisconsin win against Minnesota AND a UCLA loss against USC AND an Oregon loss to Washington AND a win by one of Northwestern (vs. Illinois), Penn State (vs. Maryland), or Rutgers (vs. Michigan State) How USC clinches a Big Ten berth Update (Friday afternoon): Iowa’s win also eliminated USC. Every path for USC to the title game required Iowa to lose to Nebraska. Previously: Finally, here is how the Trojans can head to the Big Ten Championship Game: A win against UCLA AND a loss by Indiana against Purdue AND a loss by Iowa against Nebraska AND a loss by Ohio State against Michigan AND a loss by Oregon against Washington AND a loss by Wisconsin against Minnesota, OR A win against UCLA AND an Ohio State win against Michigan AND a Wisconsin win against Minnesota AND an Indiana loss to Purdue AND an Iowa loss against Nebraska AND an Oregon loss to Washington, OR A win against UCLA AND an Ohio State win against Michigan AND a loss by Indiana against Purdue AND a loss by Iowa against Nebraska AND an Oregon loss against Washington AND a Wisconsin loss against Minnesota, OR A win against UCLA AND a Wisconsin win against Minnesota AND an Indiana loss against Purdue AND an Iowa loss against Nebraska AND an Oregon loss to Washington AND an Ohio State loss to Michigan Big Ten tiebreakers For those wondering how the tiebreakers work in the Big Ten, the full list can be found here.

title: SEC Championship Game scenarios: Who will play Georgia?
summary: One spot in the final SEC Championship Game is set. But who will Georgia play next weekend in Atlanta? With the college football world moving to a 24-game playoff next season, the Power 4 conferences have already declared that this year’s round of conference championship games will be the last. That means the winner of […]
content: (Photo by Jeffrey Vest/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images One spot in the final SEC Championship Game is set. But who will Georgia play next weekend in Atlanta? With the college football world moving to a 24-game playoff next season, the Power 4 conferences have already declared that this year’s round of conference championship games will be the last. That means the winner of the SEC Championship Game this year will have bragging rights for the near future, or until the sport changes yet again. Georgia has already clinched one spot in that game, but who will take on the Bulldogs in Atlanta? As Rivalry Week begins three teams — Texas, Tennessee, and Alabama — are fighting for that final spot. Here is how each can book a ticket to Atlanta. SEC standings Here is how the top four teams stack up in the SEC ahead of Rivalry Week: 1. Georgia (10-1 overall, 8-1 in conference) 2. Texas (9-2 overall, 6-2 in conference) 3. Tennessee (9-2 overall, 6-2 in conference) 4. Alabama (9-2 overall, 6-2 in conference) How Texas clinches an SEC berth Here is how the Longhorns can clinch a spot in the SEC Championship Game: A win against Texas A&M and an Alabama loss to Auburn, OR A win against Texas A&M and a Tennessee loss to Vanderbilt, OR A win against Texas A&M and a loss by EITHER LSU against Arkansas OR Mississippi State against Ole Miss How Tennessee clinches an SEC berth Here is how the Volunteers can punch their ticket to Atlanta: A win over Vanderbilt AND a Texas loss against Texas A&M, OR A loss by Alabama against Auburn AND a loss by Texas against Texas A&M AND a loss by Oklahoma against Missouri How Alabama clinches an SEC berth Here is how Alabama can book a trip to the final SEC Championship Game: A win against Auburn AND a Tennessee loss against Vanderbilt AND a Texas loss against Texas A&M, OR A win against Auburn AND a Tennessee win against Vanderbilt AND a Texas win against Texas A&M AND an LSU win against Arkansas AND a Mississippi State win against Ole Miss, OR A Tennessee loss against Vanderbilt AND a Texas loss against Texas A&M AND a Missouri loss against Oklahoma SEC tiebreakers Here is the full list of tiebreakers in the SEC , per the conference Using these, here are a few scenarios to know. If Tennessee loses and Texas and Alabama both win to improve to 7-2 in conference play, then Texas would move on to the SEC title game. Why? Under the above tiebreakers Texas would have a common conference opponent tiebreaker thanks to a win over Tennessee, as the Volunteers beat Alabama. If there is a two-way tie between Tennessee and Alabama, then Tennessee moves onto the title game thanks to a head-to-head win over Alabama. If there is a two-way tie between Texas and Tennessee, then Texas heads to the title game, thanks to a head-to-head win over the Volunteers. This means that if Texas wins on Friday night against Texas A&M, then the Volunteers are effectively eliminated from the SEC Championship Game. title: NFL playoff picture: What does the Bills’ win over the Chiefs mean for AFC standings?
summary: Update: Buffalo’s dramatic win over Kansas City on Thanksgiving night kept the Bills atop the AFC standings, and Buffalo is now two games ahead of No. 2 seed Denver for the moment. Kansas City remains in the No. 5 spot, and the Chiefs are one game behind the Broncos in the loss column for the […]
content: (Photo by Ryan Kang/Getty Images) | Getty Images Update: Buffalo’s dramatic win over Kansas City on Thanksgiving night kept the Bills atop the AFC standings, and Buffalo is now two games ahead of No. 2 seed Denver for the moment. Kansas City remains in the No. 5 spot, and the Chiefs are one game behind the Broncos in the loss column for the moment. Two AFC titans renew their rivalry on Thanksgiving night, when Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills host Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs. With both teams near the top of the AFC standings, this game has serious playoff implications for both teams and the AFC as a whole. Let’s dive into the playoff scenarios for both the Bills and the Chiefs ahead of this game. AFC playoff standings Here is the AFC standings ahead of Week 12: 1. Buffalo Bills (9-1) 2. Denver Broncos (8-2) 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3) 4. Cincinnati Bengals (7-3) 5. Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) 6. Cleveland Browns (6-4) 7. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-4) 8. New England Patriots (5-5) 9. Houston Texans (4-6) 10. Las Vegas Raiders (4-7) 11. Baltimore Ravens (4-7) 12. New York Jets (3-8) 13. Indianapolis Colts (3-8) 14. Los Angeles Chargers (1-9) 15. Miami Dolphins (1-9) 16. Tennessee Titans (1-9) Buffalo Bills playoff picture With a 9-1 record, the Bills sit atop the AFC standings and in position for the No. 1 seed in the conference, as well as the lone bye week. Buffalo also has a comfortable four-game lead over the New England Patriots in the AFC East, but New England won their meeting earlier this season. Should Buffalo win on Thursday night, the Bills would improve to 10-1 and maintain control of the top spot in the conference. A loss, however, would drop Buffalo down to the No. 2 line, and put Kansas City in control of the top seed, at least for the moment. Kansas City Chiefs playoff picture If the NFL playoffs began today, the Kansas City Chiefs would be in, but as the No. 5 seed in the AFC. Why? That comes down to tiebreakers. The Chiefs are tied with the Denver Broncos with an 8-2 record, and those two teams have already split their season series. Since both teams are 3-1 in AFC West games, under the league’s tiebreaking procedures, the next step is win-loss-tied percentage in common games. Both teams have defeated the Las Vegas Raiders, while the Chiefs lost to the Seattle Seahawks, a team the Broncos beat. So for the moment, the Broncos are ahead in the AFC West, and they take the No. 2 spot. However, the Chiefs would not only take control of the top spot in the division, but they would move to the top spot in the AFC overall with a win on Thursday night. That would pull Kansas City level with Buffalo, and the Chiefs would have a head-to-head tiebreaker advantage over the Bills with the victory. With a loss, the Chiefs would remain in the No. 5 spot. They would not be in danger of sliding down further, as both the Cleveland Browns and the Pittsburgh Steelers — the teams at No. 6 and No. 7 right now — are 6-4. But the Chiefs would be on the wrong end of the head-to-head tiebreaker with Buffalo. Tiebreaker implications The winner of this game will have a head-to-head tiebreaker advantage, which is the first step in deciding tiebreakers between division winners when it comes to seeding.

title: NFL survivor picks, strategy: Week 12 safe, value, and trap options
summary: Happy Thanksgiving! Even if you don’t celebrate the holiday, you know that it means a Thursday tripleheader of NFL action. The NFL has added a Black Friday game in recent years and now we also get a Wednesday game because the NFL clearly needs more revenue. Last week was a relatively quiet one, with few […]
content: (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Happy Thanksgiving! Even if you don’t celebrate the holiday, you know that it means a Thursday tripleheader of NFL action. The NFL has added a Black Friday game in recent years and now we also get a Wednesday game because the NFL clearly needs more revenue. Last week was a relatively quiet one, with few competitive matchups and the best game of the week, Vikings vs. 49ers in Mexico City, ending up a lopsided Niners win. The hope is this week brings something a little better, and the matchups on tap suggest it should. The week opens on Wednesday with two 6-4 squads as the Rams host the Packers. Thanksgiving brings us a huge NFC matchup between the Bears and Lions and a huge AFC matchup between the Chiefs and Bills. Black Friday features Broncos-Steelers with AFC seeding implications. Sunday brings Seahawks-49ers, and we close things out with the NFC South on Monday featuring Panthers vs. Buccaneers in Tampa. Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and comments Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . I’m back with my Week 12 Survivor picks on Wednesday ahead of Packers-Rams. Survivor involves picking one team each week to win. If they win you advance, if they lose you’re out in most cases. I’m in one pool with four entries, but it’s also a double-elimination pool. I’m down to one entry that has one strike against it, but I’m hanging around for now. Below I’ve got a look at the safest choices, best value picks, and then trap picks. I’ll post my own picks at the end. I’ll update on Sunday once I lock in my three picks for the weekend. I’ve included odds for the favorite in each game, courtesy of FanDuel . Safest picks Jaguars (-14.5) over Titans Bengals (-9.5) over Saints The Jaguars are the biggest favorite this week, and it’s not close. The Bengals are the second biggest favorites and with the Saints struggling, they should roll. Best value picks Cowboys (-8.5) over Eagles Jaguars (-14.5) over Titans Commanders (-7) over Cardinals Cowboys over Eagles is very much a trap game (see below), but at this stage of the season, there’s value in them if you wanna get a little nuts. The only game you might use them is Week 17 at home against the Giants, but that would be arguably a wilder pick given the Giants performances this season. Avoid this pick if you can, but there’s some value if you are in a pickle. The Jaguars offer some value late in the season, traveling to face a bad Colts team in Week 18, but that’s a long ways off. First, you might not even make it to Week 18. Second, who knows what the Jaguars will or won’t have to play for and if they’ll even be playing starters. If you have them available, now is the week. UPDATE : I forgot about the Commanders game in Arizona. You’re probably not using Washington again this season and this is a good week if you want to save the Jaguars. Trap pick Cowboys (-8.5) over Eagles While there is some value, this is a tricky one given the divisional nature, the Eagles coming off a spicy win over the Steelers, and it being Thanksgiving. And the Cowboys remain a questionable option most weeks. My picks this week I’m rolling with the Jaguars. UPDATE : Scratch that, I’m going with the Commanders. I want to save the Jaguars for December, so we’ll roll the dice with Washington. It’s a road game, but Arizona stinks.

title: Tom Brady’s call of the Eagles’ Thanksgiving game-winning FG might be the greatest ever
summary: Tom Brady is arguably the greatest quarterback in NFL history. He’s also a minority owner of the Las Vegas Raiders, and the holder of the largest broadcasting contract ever to call games for FOX Sports. Brady was working on Thanksgiving to call the Philadelphia Eagles vs. Dallas Cowboys matchup, which was clearly the worst game […]
content: Tom Brady is arguably the greatest quarterback in NFL history. He’s also a minority owner of the Las Vegas Raiders, and the holder of the largest broadcasting contract ever to call games for FOX Sports . Brady was working on Thanksgiving to call the Philadelphia Eagles vs. Dallas Cowboys matchup, which was clearly the worst game of the Turkey Day slate. The Eagles have been a legitimate trainwreck this year, while the Cowboys just can’t stop shooting themselves in the foot. Fans who thought they could take a nap during Cowboys-Eagles made a huge mistake. This somehow turned into one of the most exciting games of the NFL season, and Brady made a call on the game-winning play that might just eventually come to define his broadcasting career. The Eagles beat the Cowboys, 39-38, to erase a three-touchdown deficit on the final play of the game. Jake Elliott kicked a game-winning 59-yard field goal just before time expired in the fourth quarter, and Brady was ready for the moment. Please listen to the call from Kevin Burkhardt and Brady on Elliott’s kick. This is the greatest call I have ever heard in my life man 😭😭😭 pic.twitter.com/EtLZUTdQqv https://t.co/slKKLkE2cT — Cam (@42Cyc) November 27, 2026 Yes, that’s Tom Brady moaning as the kick sails through the uprights. I can’t stop watching this video, and I can’t stop laughing. After he composed himself, Brady said Elliott “absolutely nuts one right down the pipe.” That’s what it sounded like, Tom. Tom Brady saying “absolutely nuts one right down the pipe” is INSANE 😭 pic.twitter.com/rnZdh2ni5e — NFL Memes (@NFLMemes) November 27, 2026 Brady was in awe of Eagles QB Joe Milton the entire game. Milton — who was filling in for the injured Jalen Hurts — is known for his ridiculous throwing power, and Brady was truly losing his mind watching Milton lead the comeback . The Cowboys had better than a 97% chance to win this game with under five minutes left. Somehow, they blew it again, and the Eagles came away with a win they will never forget. Brady’s call made the kick even better. The GOAT has gotten progressively better in the booth now midway through his third ceiling, and calling Elliott’s kick might be his best moment yet.

title: NFL Thanksgiving Winners & Losers
summary: Thanksgiving football rocked. It’s not every year we get to say that the NFL gave us three incredible games, but here we are. The midday slugfest in the NFC North gave us a game that went down to the wire between the Bears and Lions, the incredible way the Cowboys managed to blow it against […]
content: (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images Thanksgiving football rocked. It’s not every year we get to say that the NFL gave us three incredible games, but here we are. The midday slugfest in the NFC North gave us a game that went down to the wire between the Bears and Lions, the incredible way the Cowboys managed to blow it against the Eagles, and the wild weather in Chiefs-Bills gave us a little bit of everything. In every game there are winners and losers, and today we celebrate them. Winner: Caleb Williams It was a team victory for the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving, as they surged into 1st place in the NFC North — but this was one of those big-time gut-check games for Caleb Williams at QB. Going into Ford Field and beating Detroit is tough work, and to do it in a national game with all eyes on you is mighty impressive. The NFC North will depend on divisional victories, and he the Bears are in a great position now to close out the season strong. Loser: Detroit Lions You can’t cough up an 11 point lead with two minutes left in the game — it’s that simple. The Jared Goff interception was bad, no doubt about it, but the true backbreaker at the close of the game was Anthony Lucas getting flagged for taunting to start off the drive. It was an unnecessary 15-yard loss at one of the most critical points of the game. While you could hand-wave it away and say, “It wouldn’t have changed the outcome,” consider what an extra 15 yards would have meant to the Bears on the ensuing drive. If everything played out the same, then when Goff is picked, the ball is at the Chicago 18-yard line to start the drive. There is a mammoth psychological difference between needing to drive 80 yards to win, and needing to gain 65 yards. There would have been more pressure on throwing the ball deeper, and every play becomes more urgent. The Lions have given up the top of the NFC North. They blew it. Winner: Joe Milton I don’t know what the long-term future is for the Eagles at quarterback, but Milton’s performance on Thanksgiving is going to lead to some uncomfortable conversations. I don’t think he’s a perfect quarterback by any stretch of the imagination, but he’s certainly close enough to Jalen Hurts that it’s increasingly difficult to justify paying a QB $51M AAV, when there’s someone playing equally well you could pay much, much less. Milton played solid football and didn’t let the moment get too big for him. This is also a guy who is on a one year, $1 million contract — and now there are going to be teams putting him on their free agent list. There’s a lot of football to go, but that was a statement game. Loser: The Cowboys, obviously There is nothing left to say. I just feel badly for Dak Prescott who routinely seems like the only guy on that team who really cares. Winner: Mother Nature I’m not going to pretend that the last game was a barn burner. We saw the Chiefs and Bills at their absolute worst because of the conditions, which rendered the game a sloppy mess. I’m not going to wax poetic about needing to homogenize football, but there’s no doubt the weather stole a really good game from us. Loser: Harrison Butker The Chiefs would have been better off if Harrison Butker stayed in the kitchen this Thanksgiving.

title: The Goo Goo Dolls’ halftime show was cut by NBC, and fans were blaming the same person
summary: The 2026 NFL Thanksgiving slate delivered in almost every way possible. Fans were treated to three amazing games that all came down to the buzzer. The Chicago Bears started the day with a wild comeback against the Detroit Lions, the Philadelphia Eagles pulled off an even more unlikely comeback to stun the Dallas Cowboys and […]
content: The 2026 NFL Thanksgiving slate delivered in almost every way possible. Fans were treated to three amazing games that all came down to the buzzer. The Chicago Bears started the day with a wild comeback against the Detroit Lions, the Philadelphia Eagles pulled off an even more unlikely comeback to stun the Dallas Cowboys and broadcaster Tom Brady, and then the Buffalo Bills beat the Kansas City Chiefs on a walk-off 57-yard field goal in the nightcap. It wasn’t just the football that was great: the NFL also lined up three killer halftime shows after the league set up a killer U2 halftime set during the Thanksgiving Eve game between the Rams and Packers. Wu-Tang Clan was incredible as the halftime act for Bears-Lions, Miranda Lambert aced her performance during the Cowboys vs. Eagles, and then the Goo Goo Dolls delivered an epic halftime show during the Chiefs-Bills game. There was only one problem: audiences missed most of the Goo Goo Dolls’ set because NBC opted to show an interview with Mike Tomlin on the outrageous Aaron Rodgers situation that led to his release from the Pittsburgh Steelers this week. Tomlin coached Rodgers in Pittsburgh a year ago for the last of his 19 seasons as head coach of the franchise. Sure, Tomlin has some unique perspective on the situation, but fans really wanted to see the Goo Goo Dolls. When NBC finally cut to the halftime show, the band killed it in the middle of their signature hit “Iris.” It’s a shame the band didn’t even get two minutes of air time. Watch their brief performance here: The Goo Goo Dolls perform Iris in the rain at Highmark‼️ pic.twitter.com/VaO2lQObCP — TSN (@TSN_Sports) November 27, 2026 Audiences were treated to the full halftime shows from Wu-Tang Clan and Lambert, so they thought they would be getting the whole set from the Goo Goo Dolls, not just 90 seconds. With rain falling down in Buffalo, this should have been the perfect backdrop for a great set. If only all of America could have seen it. The videos from inside the stadium looked fantastic: 🚨BREAKING: A FAN IN ATTENDANCE JUST POSTED FOOTAGE OF MOST OF THE GOO GOO DOLLS’ LEGENDARY THANKSGIVING HALFTIME SHOW IN BUFFALO. NBC only aired about 30 seconds of the performance, leaving millions of viewers furious. Here is what NBC did not show us: pic.twitter.com/dWMK2C940J — MLFootball (@MLFootball) November 27, 2026 The goo goo dolls are fire pic.twitter.com/j90DVrHlwJ — Chelsea✌🏻 (@BuffaloBossBabe) November 27, 2026 There have now been several full days of 24/7 Aaron Rodgers talk on every sports station imaginable. Did we really need to interrupt a great halftime show to keep talking about a washed up, 40-something QB? Fans were furious that they missed most of the Goo Goo Dolls’ set — and some of them were blaming Rodgers. Here’s a sampling of the conversation on social media: ok but what if i wanted to hear “iris” by the goo goo dolls in the rain? https://t.co/qG1NiRLQNR — kennedi landry (@kennlandry) November 27, 2026 Aaron Rodgers ruins one last thing as NBC airs Tomlin interview instead of Goo Goo Dolls concert — mr. lawyer guy (@jasonbeahm) November 27, 2026 Aaron Rodgers took away Iris by the goo goo dolls from us all. Enough of him! — Jordan (@jordancicchelli) November 27, 2026 As one last f you to us all, Aaron Rodgers has ruined the Goo Goo Dolls. Thanks, Aaron. https://t.co/mr49gcpQNS — rachel (@rachellynneb) November 27, 2026 Aaron Rodgers ruined the Goo Goo Dolls concert. Bad guy. — Chuck Naso (@ChuckNaso) November 27, 2026 I feel entitled to compensation for only getting 45 seconds of the Goo Goo Dolls while every other halftime show has aired in full. — Clif Turner (@clif_turner) November 27, 2026 I will never forgive NBC for this grave injustice https://t.co/NnRqJI9s6S — Anthony Dabbundo (@AnthonyDabbundo) November 27, 2026 I can’t believe we only got 20 seconds of Goo Goo Dolls. Heads need to roll at NBC — Pranav Tadikonda (@pranavtad) November 27, 2026 They are a great band. That was badly handled and disrespectful. https://t.co/4dNCUHgBp0 — Stevie Van Zandt (@StevieVanZandt) November 27, 2026 Aaron Rodgers has already stolen so much attention from sports fans. Did he need to steal the Goo Goo Dolls, too? The Goo Goo Dolls’ rain-soaked performance in Buffalo over a decade ago is considered an instant classic. This should have been the encore the band deserved — but NBC refused to give fans what they wanted. Less Aaron Rodgers and more Goo Goo Dolls would be good for everyone. If only the network television executives would have realized it.

title: NFL playoff picture: Steelers boost chances with Week 12 win over Broncos
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers overcame a wild week of Aaron Rodgers hubbub to beat the Denver Broncos 27-5 on Black Friday and boost their playoff chances. Pittsburgh improved to 7-4 with the win while Denver dropped to 8-3 with the loss. Heading into the game, most of the chatter was around the release of Aaron Rodgers. […]
content: (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers overcame a wild week of Aaron Rodgers hubbub to beat the Denver Broncos 27-5 on Black Friday and boost their playoff chances. Pittsburgh improved to 7-4 with the win while Denver dropped to 8-3 with the loss. Heading into the game, most of the chatter was around the release of Aaron Rodgers. The Steelers released the QB after he blasted head coach Mike McCarthy on Wednesday. That meant Mason Rudolph was getting the start at home against Bo Nix and the favored Broncos. The Steelers won primarily due to their defense, scoring two defensive touchdowns while Nix struggled all afternoon. Pittsburgh moved up the playoff standings with the win, climbing into sixth place for the time-being. They are a half game up on the Browns for the second wild card berth, pending the outcome of the Browns home game against the Raiders this weekend on Sunday Night Football . They moved to within a half game of the Bengals, who are hosting the Saints on Sunday. Denver dropped into a tie with Kansas City in the AFC West standings. The Chiefs lost to the Bills on Thanksgiving and the Broncos lost an opportunity to take a full game lead on the Chiefs and negate the tiebreakers. However, for the time-being, Denver has the edge due to the common games tiebreaker. They are 4-0 while Kansas City is 3-1.
